ledger.claim: The 3.57 km excess is read off EV-GPS-00107, which the pre-pass admits at weight 0.30 with issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED: a 331.8 m multipath jump at 21:44:57 on the Raffles Place approach, implying 193.6 kph into the outlier and 238.9 kph out of it, inside the very polyline from which the excess is measured, with no drift-corrected figure anywhere in the record. I disclose that impairment. That artifact is also the only carrier of the threshold fact — POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, and the fare meter is derived from the same trace — so under POL-GEN-02(2) the Judge's confidence cannot exceed 0.30, below the 0.70 platform floor, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation rather than a final ruling, with the disputed sum held rather than refunded. I accept that the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 seconds, a jump under 500 m, a 10-second sampling interval); this is a confidence cap, not a data failure, and the two things must be said separately.

No traffic advisory was issued for the CTE on the evening of 18 July 2026: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact, and the driver's contemporaneous explanation in the chat ('cte very jam tonight boss') is a general assertion that traffic was bad and cannot discharge his burden under POL-RD-08. He does not ask the tribunal to invent an advisory and does not press POL-RD-03. But a closure defence asserted where the only artifact that could carry it is missing from the pool is exactly the trigger in POL-RD-10(5), and the missing artifact carries nothing adverse to him either: on this record the traffic is unknown, not exculpatory, and the answer is a human reviewer, not a refund.

The rider's 60-day record is five deviation claims with one substantiated, which engages POL-RD-08's corroboration requirement because the excess here is 25.5%, below the 30% line: the claim then needs corroboration beyond the gps_trace from the POL-RD-07(ii) list. Every distance figure the rider can point to is a copy or a meter reading of the platform's single distance measurement — 17.6 km on the trip record is the rounded convenience copy POL-RD-01 forbids citing, and 17.6 km on the fare breakdown is the same measurement on the meter. The driver's own statement admits the route, but the route has never been in dispute; it supplies no independent measurement of the excess, which is what the rider must corroborate.

The rider's complaint folds the 1.35 surge multiplier — SGD 9.28 of the SGD 36.60 charged — into the loss. The multiplier is a booking-time line recorded only on the fare breakdown and is not a consequence of the route driven; POL-RD-02 applies it to the recomputed optimal-route fare, so it cannot be presented as deviation damage.

The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty), no tolls (tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. There is accordingly no pass-through correction and no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge for POL-RD-09 to add on top of any distance figure, and the rider's exposure is confined to the distance-and-time line alone.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The ride from Ang Mo Kio to Raffles Place on the night of 18 July 2026 deviated from the platform's optimal route, and part of the fare is returned.

The route. The optimal route for this booking was 14.0 km (CTE southbound throughout, per the trip record's routing engine). The driver's GPS polyline measures 17.57 km, an excess of 3.57 km, or 25.5% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on the trace figure, which governs over the rounded 17.6 km copy. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (that needs over 50% or over 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral.

The GPS trace. I say two things about EV-GPS-00107. It is impaired at the schema level: admissibility weight 0.30, issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath jump on the final Raffles Place approach, implying 193.6 kph into and 238.9 kph out of the outlier). But it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: there is no gap over 90 s (no gaps at all), the worst jump is 331.8 m (under the 500 m limb), and the sampling interval is a steady 10 s. So a deviation may be, and is, established on it, and the finding survives the 0.30 discount because it is independently carried.

Corroboration. Because the rider's 60-day record shows 5 deviation claims with 1 substantiated, and the excess here is under 30%, POL-RD-08 requires corroboration beyond the GPS trace. It exists. The driver's own chat reply to the rider's challenge ('why exit at whitley?') -- 'cte very jam tonight boss' -- concedes that he left the CTE, and the driver's statement on file admits the route outright ('I went by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it'). Both are on the POL-RD-07(ii) list that POL-RD-08 borrows, and POL-RD-08 does not require the corroboration to re-measure the excess; a driver admission of the route is exactly what it names.

The driver's escalation argument. I do not accept that the 0.30 trace is the sole carrier of the deciding fact. The deviation is independently carried by the driver's chat admission on EV-CHAT-00107 (weight 1.0), so under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is the MAXIMUM of the independent carriers (1.0), not the minimum, and the 0.70 floor is not crossed. The counterparty statement is evidence and satisfies the corroboration limb, but it carries no weight and so does not itself set the cap.

The missing advisory. No traffic advisory was issued for the CTE that evening, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing and no closure-adjusted optimal can be built. The driver's 'it was jammed' is a general assertion unsupported by any advisory; under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the burden of excusing the deviation, so the 3.57 km excess stands. That is a failure of the defence, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact (the driver's side expressly did not press POL-RD-03), and POL-RD-08 is the clause that governs an unsupported traffic assertion.

Other points. POL-RD-04 does not apply: there was no rider instruction (waypoint_hint is null and no road is named), and the chat message was a challenge, not a request. POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-02 governs. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo discount. The 1.35 surge is a booking-time line applied to the recomputed optimal fare, not refunded as deviation damage.

The refund (POL-RD-02) is arithmetic. Charged total 36.60. Recomputed optimal-route fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 platform fee = (21.02 x 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177. Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to SGD 7.45. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of the charged total, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 7.45. The charge is presently on the rider (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); this order reverses SGD 7.45 of it.
